## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of Gatekeeper policy design, basic Rego, and CI validation.

## Key Concepts
- OPA Gatekeeper, ConstraintTemplate, Constraint, Rego basics
- Pod security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, image allowlists
- CI integration and local validation strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (conceptual)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8spodsecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8SPodSecurity
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8spodsecurity
      # policy consolidated in real template
```
```yaml
# Constraint (conceptual)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8SPodSecurity
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: ["apps"]
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
  parameters:
    allowList:
      - registry.example.com/*
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle per-environment allowlists?
- How would you audit Gatekeeper decisions historically?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests understanding of Helm templating and basic policy checks in CI for secure defaults, plus ability to craft a simple gate that a junior engineer can implement.

## Key Concepts

- Helm templating and values.yaml
- YAML validation with yq
- Kubernetes securityContext basics
- Image tag policy and registry scoping
- CI gate design and test manifests

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/helm-gate.yml
name: Helm gate
on: push
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: azure/setup-helm@v1
      - name: Render charts
        run: helm template mychart charts/mychart > /tmp/rendered.yaml
      - name: Validate images
        run: |
          if ! yq e '.items[].spec.template.spec.containers[].image' /tmp/rendered.yaml | grep -q registry.example.com/secure/; then echo image origin invalid; exit 1; fi
```

```yaml
# failing Deployment manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: registry.example.com/secure/myservice:latest
          # missing securityContext and resources
```

```yaml
# passing Deployment manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: registry.example.com/secure/myservice:v1.2.3
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 200m
              memory: 256Mi
```

- How would you extend to multi-container pods?
- How would you adapt for multiple charts in a single repo?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical gate design for multi-tenant environments with real tooling and secrets handling.

## Key Concepts
- Cosign signature verification against a repository public key
- Digest pinning and non-latest image references in manifests/Helm

## Code Example
```yaml
name: gate-ci
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup cosign
        run: |
          cosign version
          cosign verify -key cosign.pub registry.example.com/namespace/service@digest
      - name: Lint manifests & charts
        run: |
          helm lint charts/
          yq eval '(.spec.template.spec.containers[].image) != ""' manifests/**/*.yaml
      - name: Validate Vault refs
        run: |
          echo "Vault refs resolved and projected secrets configured" 
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate the cosign key and propagate it to pipelines?
- How would you detect drift between SBOMs and deployed images at runtime?

## Why This Is Asked

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to express policy-as-code for security/compliance in multi-cloud clusters, combining network isolation, identity controls, and outbound security.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper/OPA ConstraintTemplate
- NetworkPolicy as runtime guard
- Pod securityContext and automountServiceAccountToken control
- mTLS and central CA validation for outbound traffic
- CI verification using kubectl, gatekeeper audits

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8snetworkidentity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sNetworkIdentityConstraint
  targets:
  - target: Kubernetes
    rego: |
      package k8snetworkidentity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind == "Deployment"
        not has_ns_deny_ingress(input)
        msg := "Deployment namespace must have a deny-ingress NetworkPolicy and allow only whitelisted sources."
      }
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (no deny ingress and automount enabled)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-fail
  namespace: dev
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: example-fail
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: example-fail
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (deny ingress, trusted SA, automount disabled)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: app-sa
  namespace: dev
  annotations:
    trusted.example.io: "true"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-pass
  namespace: dev
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: example-pass
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: example-pass
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: app-sa
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

```yaml
# Minimal NetworkPolicy (deny ingress by default, allow from trusted namespace)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-ingress
  namespace: dev
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          env: trusted
```

## CI Verification Steps
- Gatekeeper audit run in CI to ensure constraints are evaluated.
- kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f failing.yaml should trigger policy violations.
- kubectl apply -f passing.yaml should succeed and Gatekeeper should record no violations.
- Validate that namespaces have the required NetworkPolicy objects and that deployments use trusted SAs with automountServiceAccountToken disabled.

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to create simple, deterministic CI gates focused on security hygiene in manifests, with minimal tooling. Shows understanding of Kubernetes volumes, YAML parsing, and CI integration.

## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes hostPath security risks
- Manifest scanning with lightweight parsers (yq, Python)
- GitHub Actions workflow basics
- Local verification of a detector script

## Code Example

```python
# detector.py
import sys, yaml
def has_hostpath(path):
  data = yaml.safe_load(open(path))
  vols = data.get('spec', {}).get('volumes', []) or []
  for v in vols:
    if 'hostPath' in v:
      return True
  return False
if __name__ == '__main__':
  ok = True
  for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    if has_hostpath(f):
      ok = False
      print('HOSTPATH found in', f)
  sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Fintech workloads handling sensitive financial data demand strict data-protection posture. This question validates your understanding of end-to-end security enforcement—from CI gates that catch misconfigurations before deployment to runtime policies that protect running workloads.

## Key Concepts
- CI gate for manifest validation at pull request stage
- Resource requests/limits for resource governance
- readOnlyRootFilesystem for filesystem security
- TLS secret mounting with tls-cert-<app> naming convention
- Runtime policy enforcement via Kyverno or OPA
- Verification strategies for both CI and cluster runtime

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-deploy
spec:
  rules:
  - name: enforce-resources-readonly
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "Deployment must set resources.limits, resources.requests, and readOnlyRootFilesystem: true"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              securityContext:
                readOnlyRootFilesystem: "true"
              containers:
              - resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
                  requests:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
  - name: enforce-tls-secret-mount
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: "TLS secret must be mounted at /etc/tls from Secret tls-cert-<app>"
      pattern:
        spec:
          volumes:
          - secret:
              secretName: tls-cert-?*
              items:
              - key: tls.crt
                path: etc/tls/tls.crt
```

## Sample Compliant Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tls-cert-payment-service
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  tls.crt: <base64-cert>
  tls.key: <base64-key>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payment-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      securityContext:
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: payment-service:latest
        resources:
          limits:
            memory: "512Mi"
            cpu: "500m"
          requests:
            memory: "256Mi"
            cpu: "250m"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls-certs
          mountPath: /etc/tls
          readOnly: true
      volumes:
      - name: tls-certs
        secret:
          secretName: tls-cert-payment-service
```

## Sample Non-Compliant Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: insecure-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: insecure-service:latest
        # Missing: resources.limits/requests
        # Missing: readOnlyRootFilesystem
        # Missing: TLS secret mount
```

## GitHub Actions CI Gate
```yaml
name: Security Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  security-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - name: Install kubeval
      run: |4
        curl -L -o kubeval https://github.com/instrumenta/kubeval/releases/latest/download/kubeval-linux-amd64.tar.gz
        tar xf kubeval-linux-amd64.tar.gz
        sudo mv kubeval /usr/local/bin
    - name: Validate manifests
      run: |
        for f in k8s/*.yaml; do
          kubeval --strict --additional-schema-locations=https://kubernetesjsonschema.dev $f || exit 1
        done
    - name: Check resource limits
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].resources.limits' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
    - name: Check readOnlyRootFilesystem
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem == true' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
    - name: Check TLS secret mounting
      run: |
        yq -e '.spec.template.spec.volumes[].secret.secretName | test("^tls-cert-")' k8s/*.yaml || exit 1
```

## Verification Steps

### CI Verification
1. Create a PR with the non-compliant manifest—pipeline should fail
2. Update to compliant manifest—pipeline should pass
3. Confirm all three checks (resources, readOnlyRootFilesystem, TLS) are enforced

### Runtime Verification
1. Apply Kyverno policy to test cluster
2. Attempt to deploy non-compliant manifest—deployment should be blocked
3. Verify policy logs show rejection reason
4. Apply compliant manifest—deployment should succeed

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical expertise in multi-tenant security, using real-world tools (cosign, Rekor, Kyverno, KMS) to enforce image provenance at CI time. It emphasizes tenant isolation, key management, and concrete verification steps.

## Key Concepts
- Cosign-based image signing with per-tenant keys stored in a central KMS
- Rekor-backed provenance verification
- Kyverno policy enforcing signatures and digest pinning across repos
- CI gating via GitHub Actions, plus local verification workflow

## Code Example
```yaml
# GitHub Actions gate (high level)
name: Image Signatures Gate
on: pull_request
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install cosign
        run: curl -fsSL https://toolkit.cosign.is/cosign-linux-amd64 -o /usr/local/bin/cosign && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/cosign
      - name: Fetch tenant key from KMS
        run: |
          echo "Fetching tenant key..." # placeholder
      - name: Verify images in manifests
        run: |
          cosign verify --key <tenant-key> image digest
```
```yaml
# Kyverno policy snippet (digest-signature & tag checks)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-cosign-signature
spec:
  rules:
  - name: image-signature
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment, Job, KnativeService]
    validate:
      message: "Image must be cosign-signed with tenant key"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: ?*
              - imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate tenant keys without downtime?
- How would you audit failures and respond to a signature mismatch in production?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical understanding of Kubernetes NetworkPolicy default-deny behavior and namespace isolation.

## Key Concepts
- NetworkPolicy basics and default-deny
- Namespace isolation and namespace selectors
- Ingress vs Egress rules

## Code Example
```yaml
# policy.yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-cross-namespace
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: tenant-a
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: tenant-a
```

```yaml
# compliant-pod.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: p-a-compliant
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  containers:
  - name: curl
    image: curlimages/curl:8.88.0
    command: ["sh","-c","curl -s http://tenant-a-service.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local:80/health || true"]
```

```yaml
# noncompliant-pod.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: p-a-cross
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  containers:
  - name: curl
    image: curlimages/curl:8.88.0
    command: ["sh","-c","curl -s http://tenant-b-service.tenant-b.svc.cluster.local:80/health || true"]
```

```bash
# verification plan
kubectl apply -f policy.yaml
kubectl apply -f compliant-pod.yaml
kubectl apply -f noncompliant-pod.yaml
# test within tenant-a
kubectl logs p-a-compliant -n tenant-a
# cross-namespace should fail
kubectl logs p-a-cross -n tenant-a
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this for namespace-label-based multi-tenant isolation?
- What changes if using Calico instead of default k8s NetworkPolicy support?
